title: Amazed At My Progress in 7 Days
author: PykeTheTitan
selftext:
This is a demo of the PvE extraction game I have been working on for just over a week. Everything you see is randomly generated. I bought an asset set from Vladimir Trofimov which I love, but eventually I'm hoping AI gets good enough for me to make custom assets, it's not quite on the par I'm looking for. I'm using only GPT 5.6 Sol on medium, very rarely using thinking level higher than that.

I have massive ambition for this game and I'm not even nearly close to what I have planned. I know ambition kills games but I'm having fun and it's not something I'm willing to sacrifice. All I have done so far is just basic combat with sword and bow and some basic map generation, but like I said this is not close to what I want this game to become.

In a world of people one shotting games, I think the true advantage of ai is how quickly you can iterate. I think the best art is made through thousands of iterations and pivoting throughout the process and that was my entire approach. To get to my current stage I have done hundreds of prompts over the past week, tons of bugs and fixes. I have videos of most of the iterations so I plan to make some videos in the future showing every iteration up to certain checkpoints.

So I have 2 repositories, 1 is an obsidian vault that holds all my thoughts. A big part of creating the game I have in mind is learning, so I talk to ai all the time. On my drives to work I just talk about stuff I have implemented, plans, systems, literally anything and everything. Then I have an agent that can ingest the conversations I have with ai and sort all my thoughts into a vault so my agent always understands my project and my vision. Ai is great at implementing things but it has no taste, that is the advantage humans have. All I am in this project is a taste director. I tell Ai to implement something, go off and do other stuff. I see what it implemented, and then I write down thoughts on the changes, what they did right, and what they did wrong, and tell it what direction to iterate. I have been doing this loop constantly for the last 7 days. I can do this during work because all I have to do is reivew the changes and give GPT a new direction to iterate in.

I want to put this into a browser soon so people can test and let me know their thoughts. Please let me know what you like and don't like about what i have so far. Obviously it is far from having a complete loop right now and the bots in the game are very dumb, but I'm going to get there eventually.

My next step is working on the movement animation, making it smoother fixing posture to feel less robotic. Please let me know your thoughts!

comments.author: lostforever2011
comments.body: Looks interesting. so if i understand correctly, you both an asset pack and then got Sol Med to build that zone/level for you? if yes, what is prompt did you use please? Did it got it right in one go? or that level/map is hand built by you? thx

replies.author: PykeTheTitan
replies.body: Yeah the asset pack was just a bunch of trees, bushes, rocks and grass. It was most definitely not one prompt. I started by having it create basic terrain, with a grass texture and a randomly generated path from end to end. Then added it randomly placed trees on all the grass areas. Fine tuned a lot from there, in terms of tree size, vertical placement. Then covered the grass areas with actually grass assets so it wasn’t just a texture. Then I added more intentional foliage, it wasn’t just randomly spread, I had GPT make sure there were patches of similar foliage together. boulders will have shrubs and tall grass around to make them look better. Tons of iteration to get to the state I’m at, and still tons more to go. Also a really nice touch was having the trees sway like there is wind, really helps the immersion. Then more details like fog and a skybox

replies.body: nice thanks for sharing. I try to use Sol Med to doing something similar and it wasted my weekly limit and got something I hated lol. Which codex plana are you on? I am on $20 version.

replies.body: Haha yeah, I upgraded to pro plan last month. I have had the $20 plan for 2 years and use ai in all parts of my life already. Still I am using up the pro plan quickly, but they have been giving out a ton of resets so it has been nice. Plus they just reduced the usage rates so it has been going down slower

comments.author: DerelictCoffee
comments.body: The first week stuff went so fast and seemed like “wow this is so easy it’s amazing!” Now my game is 5 weeks old, approaching 1gb in size and I’m fine tuning bosses mobs etc. & every change is a full re-seed and simple tuning takes hours. It takes me all day to build a boss arena and fight. But I’m no longer proving concepts, I’m tuning amd polishing. I hope it’s decent and not slop but literally all I’m doing all day/ all night is play testing, tuning, and refining which some days feels glacial compared to that first week “I built a game!” high! 😭😂 For context or curiosity my game: https://derelique.itch.io/trueofvoice

comments.author: cumbiaowl
comments.body:
These darn LLMs are too good, and they're learning from all of us game-devs. So, we'll spend quite a bit of time building games using AI, then someone a a year from now someone will build a better game using LLMs trained on ours. 

I'm having a ton of fun regardless.

replies.author: PykeTheTitan
replies.body: But that’s just the thing, I’ve realize that ai can build things that have already been built. Human taste will always be an advantage. Use ai to build something that you would play

comments.author: NotYourValidation
comments.body:
Ambition doesnt kill games. Ambition and passion is the reason people used to spend days and months learning game development just to make their game. Now literal children can make full gameslop with just a prompt. AI is great, but the mess it leaves in it's wake is a shame.

The real question is, would you have the same ambition and passion if you had to do all the work yourself?

replies.author: NotYourValidation
replies.body:
"AI Art or Artist bashing" lol, okay.

You could probably use AI to explain to you what "bashing" means, because this is not it. AI Says:

No, that statement is not "bashing."

While the statement is highly critical, it targets a **technology (AI-generated content)** and a **general trend**, rather than launching a malicious or hateful attack against a specific person.

Here is a breakdown of why this falls under critique or debate rather than verbal bashing:

Why It Is Not Bashing

* **Focuses on an Industry Trend:** The speaker is arguing about the current state of game development and how AI affects the quality of games.
* **Expresses an Opinion, Not an Insult:** Using the word "gameslop" is a harsh critique of the *product* (low-quality games), but it is not a direct personal insult or name-calling aimed at a human being.
* **Invites Reflection:** The final question ("would you have the same ambition...") is a philosophical challenge about the nature of creativity and hard work, not a verbal assault.
* **Lacks Personal Malice:** Verbal bashing usually involves a relentless desire to tear someone down, humiliate them, or destroy their reputation. This quote reads more like a frustrated developer or gamer sharing a passionate perspective.
